messages:
elena: Dropping this live thread for follow-ups from today's all-hands. Ask anything about mission, positioning, market signals, or competitor strategy. I'll answer as we go.

tasha: thanks! quick one from growth: what's the one-line we should use on outbound for regulated customers?
elena: Use: 'Redwood Inference: predictable SLAs, private deployment options, and the same developer API across environments.' Keep it benefits-first.
liam: product question: are we going to call out model coverage (supported model families) in public docs or keep it in a curated catalog? customers ask about specific LLMs.
elena: We'll keep a curated model catalog public with verified performance notes and compatible deployment modes. Full internal matrix stays internal.
priyanka: from sales: do we have a hard rule on naming competitors in sales decks? some reps want permission to name-check.
elena: Internal enablement can include direct competitor comparisons. Customer-facing decks should avoid naming unless the prospect does; instead use feature/benefit contrasts.
kevin: ops: any change to the hosting-first motion? are we prioritizing Hosted signups or treating Hosted as top-of-funnel only?
elena: Hosted remains top-of-funnel for devs and PLG. For enterprise motions we push toward Dedicated/Private for contracts and SLAs. That dual motion is intentional.
liam: posture question: when customers compare us vs hyperscalers on price, do we give ballpark numbers or focus on qualitative differences? reps want a script.
elena: Give ballpark ranges for typical Dedicated configs in enablement, but lead with measurable differences: predictable unit economics, rollout controls, and private deployment. We'll publish a short script for reps.
tasha: market signals: any signal change this quarter that would pivot our messaging?
elena: Two signals: (1) customers care more about predictable cost at scale, (2) security/compliance is driving longer sales cycles but higher ACV. Messaging will tilt toward serving economics + compliance.
priyanka: competitors: do we invest in public benchmarks to win technical customers or keep proofs private?
elena: Publish high-level benchmark summaries and reproducible tests for community trust. Keep detailed lab configs private.
kevin: ops-bot: uploaded slides and recording: https://redwood/ah/1851234567
liam: roadmap ask: can leadership confirm priority order for the next release?
elena: Top three: 1) Canary + automatic rollback, 2) KV/prefix caching improvements, 3) Dedicated autoscaling and capacity guarantees.
tasha: last one: is there a short internal note we can forward to prospects about 'why Redwood' vs the large clouds?
elena: I'll post a 1-page internal note later today that reps can use. Thanks all for the thoughtful questions.
